transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood CSM); Rajiv Kumar, Laura Chen, Tom Alvarez, Priya Nair, Evan Park (Gamma Systems)

Summary:
Short kickoff to resolve DPA redlines and align on onboarding path (procurement gating, SOC2 evidence, SSO), confirm SLA expectations and pricing lane (hosted vs dedicated), and schedule technical bench for latency/residency constraints.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redline escalation path
- Security artifacts and evidence (SOC 2 / ISO / KMS)
- SLA tradeoffs and fallback policies
- Pricing approval process and cost estimates (dedicated vs hosted)
- Onboarding timeline and next steps for procurement

Transcript:
00:00 - Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for taking time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the account lead. quick roll call?
00:07 - Rajiv Kumar: Rajiv here, procurement. we got legal and security on, this call is mainly to understand where we land on the DPA and MSA exceptions.
00:14 - Laura Chen: Laura, security. we have a list of questions around encryption at rest, KMS, audit logs, and data residency.
00:20 - Tom Alvarez: Tom, eng manager. i'll be coordinating the bench and running sample traffic.
00:24 - Priya Nair: Priya, legal. we'll walk through the redlines and escalate any must-haves.
00:28 - Jordan Lee: Great. Sofia, want to do a quick intro on deployment modes?
00:32 - Sofia Patel: Yep, hi all. Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC/on-prem packages. Hosted is fastest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, Private is for regulated workloads. Important tradeoffs: hosted has shared infra but we offer strong RBAC, SSO, and artifact retention. Dedicated can be reserved capacity with SLA and custom network setup. private is doable but requires additional onboarding windows.
00:56 - Rajiv Kumar: Our procurement asked for two things: one, clear SLA and penalty language, and two, DPA that meets our corporate policy. price approval needs a break down of committed vs burst costs.
01:08 - Jordan Lee: Understood. For SLAs we can show latency targets per model class and availability commitments for Dedicated. We have template SLA language—if you have specific RTO/RPO numbers, we can map.
01:20 - Priya Nair: On the DPA, we flagged clause 5.2 on subprocessors and clause 7.1 on data deletion timelines. we need explicit assurances on KMS integration and audit logging retention for 2 years.
01:33 - Sofia Patel: For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments, and for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed KMS in supported cloud regions; audit logs are available from the console with configurable retention but longer retention is an add-on.
01:51 - Laura Chen: That last part worries us—if audit log retention is an add on, procurement will push back. we need a baseline included for enterprise customers.
01:57 - Marcus Rivera: We typically include 90-day retention in base and can offer extended retention on contract. happy to put that in the commercial summary.
02:08 - Rajiv Kumar: Pricing—our finance team wants to compare hosted variable usage vs dedicated reserved. do you have an example cost model for 3M tokens/month baseline?
02:18 - Jordan Lee: Yes, i'll draft a TCO example. Quick note: Dedicated reduces per-token cost with reserved GPUs and batching efficiency; hosted is simpler but can be costlier at scale. I'll send example spreadsheet.
02:31 - Tom Alvarez: On the tech side we have pinch points: 99th percentile latency for inference must be under 350ms for our chat product. can you meet that on hosted?
02:42 - Sofia Patel: That depends on model choice and sequence length. For many open models we can meet sub-350ms with smart routing and continuous batching, but we should run a mini-benchmark with your sample payloads to validate, also check cold-starts.
02:56 - Evan Park: Our infra requires SSO (SAML) and we have a key rotation cadence in place. also, data residency: some EU tenant data must stay in eu-west-1.
03:08 - Sofia Patel: SAML SSO is supported; we can onboard metadata and test. For regional routing we can pin requests to region. For DPA we can add explicit residency clauses.
03:20 - Priya Nair: We also escalate the subprocessors list. who are your cloud providers and third-party vendors? this is a gating concern.
03:28 - Jordan Lee: We use standard cloud providers—AWS and GCP—plus some managed CDN partners; we'll provide a subprocessors list. for Dedicated you can request a private tenancy to limit subprocessors.
03:39 - Laura Chen: SOC 2 report—can we get the latest and an attestation?
03:44 - Marcus Rivera: yes, we can share SOC 2 Type II report and our security pack via the secure link. expect that after this call.
03:50 - Priya Nair: On the MSA redlines: payment terms and audit protections are sticky points. we usually accept net-45 but with penalties and termination language around data handling.
04:01 - Jordan Lee: we'll mark those and propose commercial tradeoffs. if dedicated capacity is needed we can structure a committed spend with termination windows.
04:10 - Rajiv Kumar: Procurement timeline: we need pricing and vendor package by Jan 28 to present to spend committee Feb 2.
04:16 - Jordan Lee: Ok Jan 28 is doable if we move quickly. I'll summarize the MSA/DPA redline positions and the pricing tiers by Monday 2026-01-25.
04:24 - Tom Alvarez: For the bench, we plan a short spike—can you provide a staging environment and instructions to hit an endpoint?
04:31 - Sofia Patel: We'll spin up a test endpoint in Hosted and Dedicated staging, share runbook and sample client certs. expecting to need ~48 hours for staging setup.
04:40 - Evan Park: For on-prem/private we need a network diagram and firewall requirements to get internal approvals.
04:46 - Sofia Patel: We'll share the private deployment checklist and spatial network requirements doc.
04:52 - Laura Chen: A question—how do you handle data deletion if we terminate? we need proof of deletion within 30 days.
04:59 - Jordan Lee: We have documented deletion flows; for Private and Dedicated we can confirm tenant wipe and provide logs; for Hosted we can provide deletion attestations and options for export before termination. we'll capture that in the DPA language.
05:12 - Priya Nair: Also, please confirm no model weights from our proprietary data are retained or used for training—this must be explicit.
05:19 - Sofia Patel: Redwood's policy is no training on customer data unless contractually agreed; we'll confirm in writing and add a non-derivative clause to the DPA.
05:29 - Rajiv Kumar: Any competitors we should be aware of? we looked at Anthropic and some in-house efforts. pricing wise, Anthropic looked higher but they claimed certain latency guarantees.
05:41 - Jordan Lee: noted. we'll include a comparison table.
05:44 - Marcus Rivera: quick recap of action items and owners. Jordan will send pricing + MSA/DPA redline summary. Sofia will run tests and share runbook. Laura/Priya will send DPA redlines. Evan will provide traffic profile.
06:00 - Jordan Lee: sounds good. one last thing—can we schedule a follow up tech deep dive on Jan 29?
06:06 - Tom Alvarez: Jan 29 works for engineering—let's do afternoon.
06:10 - Jordan Lee: i'll propose times and send calendar invite. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Documents / links referenced:
- Redwood MSA template (link shared in chat)
- Redwood DPA redline tracker (Jordan to attach)
- SOC2 and security pack (Marcus will provide secure link)
- Sample pricing spreadsheet (Jordan will attach)

Closing notes:
Tone: transactional but cooperative. Key gating items: DPA subprocessors + data deletion clause, audit log retention baseline, SSO metadata, pricing TCO for hosted vs dedicated. Procurement timeline is tight (committee Feb 2).
